reciqPNnvLImSXppO.Title: Freshwater Flux from Sea-Ice Surface

reciudQt3qltmTb99.Description: vertically integrated through the atmospheric column
reciudQt3qltmTb99.Name: prw
reciudQt3qltmTb99.Title: Water Vapor Path
reciudQt3qltmTb99.Variables: CFsubhr.prw, Eday.prw, E3hr.prw, Esubhr.prw, Amon.prw, CF3hr.prw, 6hrPlevPt.prw, Amon.prwSouth30

reciv8XwrPafZyQcw.Description: negative log of hydrogen ion concentration with the concentration expressed as mol H kg-1.
reciv8XwrPafZyQcw.Name: ph
reciv8XwrPafZyQcw.Title: pH

recivgMO4TjgndWFp.Description: Upwelling clear-sky longwave radiation at top of atmosphere
recivgMO4TjgndWFp.Name: rlutcs
recivgMO4TjgndWFp.Title: TOA Outgoing Clear-Sky Longwave Radiation
recivgMO4TjgndWFp.Variables: CFsubhr.rlutcs, E1hrClimMon.rlutcs, E3hr.rlutcs, Amon.rlutcs, CFday.rlutcs, CF3hr.rlutcs, Amon.rlutcsSouth30

reciy6AhIwZIZJNxd.Description: Needed to calculate soil bulk turnover time
reciy6AhIwZIZJNxd.Name: rhSoil
reciy6AhIwZIZJNxd.Title: Carbon Mass Flux into Atmosphere Due to Heterotrophic Respiration from Soil on Land

reciysm6HHD8iNTbi.Description: "Content" indicates a quantity per unit area. "Vegetation" means any plants e.g. trees, shrubs, grass. Plants are autotrophs i.e. "producers" of biomass using carbon obtained from carbon dioxide.
reciysm6HHD8iNTbi.Name: cVegGrass
reciysm6HHD8iNTbi.Title: Carbon Mass in Vegetation on Grass Tiles

recj177YYn4e95IGS.Description: In ocean modelling, diazotrophs are phytoplankton of the phylum cyanobacteria distinct from other phytoplankton groups in their ability to fix nitrogen gas in addition to nitrate and ammonium. Phytoplankton are algae that grow where there is sufficient light to support photosynthesis. "Nitrogen growth limitation" means the ratio of the growth rate of a species population in the environment (where there is a finite availability of nitrogen) to the theoretical growth rate if there were no such limit on nitrogen availability.
recj177YYn4e95IGS.Name: limndiaz
recj177YYn4e95IGS.Title: Nitrogen Limitation of Diazotrophs

recj8H1H27CHxqcPA.Description: Growth limitation of miscellaneous phytoplankton due to solar irradiance. "Growth limitation due to solar irradiance" means the ratio of the growth rate of a species population in the environment (where the amount of sunlight reaching a location may be limited) to the theoretical growth rate if there were no such limit on solar irradiance.
recj8H1H27CHxqcPA.Name: limirrmisc
recj8H1H27CHxqcPA.Title: Irradiance Limitation of Other Phytoplankton

recj8epy9HX2qCWYc.Description: Overturning mass streamfunction arising from all advective mass transport processes, resolved and parameterized.
recj8epy9HX2qCWYc.Name: msftyz
recj8epy9HX2qCWYc.Processing Comment: For a model with a cartesian latxlon grid this should be omitted.
recj8epy9HX2qCWYc.Title: Ocean Y Overturning Mass Streamfunction

recjOdQfrMgEGFPN3.Description: Tendency of heat content for a grid cell from all processes. Reported only for models that use potential temperature as prognostic field.
recjOdQfrMgEGFPN3.Name: opottemptend
recjOdQfrMgEGFPN3.Title: Tendency of Sea Water Potential Temperature Expressed as Heat Content

recjTpDVwoQZnzjGk.Name: emibbch4
recjTpDVwoQZnzjGk.Title: total emission of CH4 from all biomass burning

recjegSTqG5eWUDhK.Description: This is the stress on the liquid ocean from overlying atmosphere, sea ice, ice shelf, etc.
recjegSTqG5eWUDhK.Name: tauuo
recjegSTqG5eWUDhK.Title: Sea Water Surface Downward X Stress

recjh4GnJXOW8OuYc.Description: Temperature of upper boundary of the liquid ocean, including temperatures below sea-ice and floating ice shelves.
recjh4GnJXOW8OuYc.Name: tosga
recjh4GnJXOW8OuYc.Title: Global Average Sea Surface Temperature

recjjacTPQpu1hYR3.Description: Percentage of entire grid cell  that is covered by anthropogenic pasture.
recjjacTPQpu1hYR3.Name: pastureFrac
recjjacTPQpu1hYR3.Title: Percentage of Land Which Is Anthropogenic Pasture

recjlnxsWLBAbmFtf.Description: Loss of soil nitrogen through remineralization and immobilisation. Remineralization is the degradation of organic matter into inorganic forms of carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus and other micronutrients, which consumes oxygen and releases energy. Immobilisation of nitrogen refers to retention of nitrogen by micro-organisms under certain conditions, making it unavailable for plants.
recjlnxsWLBAbmFtf.Name: fNnetmin
recjlnxsWLBAbmFtf.Title: Net Nitrogen Release from Soil and Litter as the Outcome of Nitrogen Immobilisation and Gross Mineralisation

recjmu4bKgUjgxLUt.Description: Sum of chlorophyll from all phytoplankton group concentrations.  In most models this is equal to chldiat+chlmisc, that is the sum of Diatom Chlorophyll Mass Concentration and Other Phytoplankton Chlorophyll Mass Concentration
recjmu4bKgUjgxLUt.Name: chl
recjmu4bKgUjgxLUt.Title: Mass Concentration of Total Phytoplankton Expressed as Chlorophyll in Sea Water

recjpcumyeHWWt56h.Description: total primary (organic carbon) production by phytoplankton
recjpcumyeHWWt56h.Name: pp
recjpcumyeHWWt56h.Title: Primary Carbon Production by Phytoplankton

recjq46Rp6k3vLWAm.Description: Tendency of heat content for a grid cell from parameterized eddy advection (any form of eddy advection). Reported only for models that use conservative temperature as prognostic field.
recjq46Rp6k3vLWAm.Name: ocontemppadvect
recjq46Rp6k3vLWAm.Title: Tendency of Sea Water Conservative Temperature Expressed as Heat Content Due to Parameterized Eddy Advection

recjsdT3H3Q1Ak12n.Description: Total NPP of trees in the grid cell
recjsdT3H3Q1Ak12n.Name: nppTree
recjsdT3H3Q1Ak12n.Title: Net Primary Production on Tree Tiles as Carbon Mass Flux [kgC m-2 s-1]

recjvhKkEsN7Erdpb.Description: "Number concentration" means the number of particles or other specified objects per unit volume. "Aerosol" means the system of suspended liquid or solid particles in air (except cloud droplets) and their carrier gas, the air itself. "Ambient\_aerosol" means that the aerosol is measured or modelled at the ambient state of pressure, temperature and relative humidity that exists in its immediate environment. "Ambient aerosol particles" are aerosol particles that have taken up ambient water through hygroscopic growth. The extent of hygroscopic growth depends on the relative humidity and the composition of the particles.
recjvhKkEsN7Erdpb.Name: conccn
recjvhKkEsN7Erdpb.Title: Aerosol Number Concentration

recjzMJa6ieFlJqcV.Name: tropch4loss
recjzMJa6ieFlJqcV.Title: Tropospheric loss of CH4 from chemical destruction

reck0W6rDk3ri9XKd.Description: It is set to zero in models which receive a real water flux.
reck0W6rDk3ri9XKd.Name: vsfcorr
reck0W6rDk3ri9XKd.Title: Virtual Salt Flux Correction

reck7Nd0K54DKgkdb.Description: The surface called "surface" means the lower boundary of the atmosphere. "Upward" indicates a vector component which is positive when directed upward (negative downward). The surface latent heat flux is the exchange of heat between the surface and the air on account of evaporation (including sublimation). In accordance with common usage in geophysical disciplines, "flux" implies per unit area, called "flux density" in physics.
reck7Nd0K54DKgkdb.Name: hflsLut
reck7Nd0K54DKgkdb.Title: Latent Heat Flux on Land-Use Tile

reckAKl91UlyUP5tT.Description: Mole fraction is used in the construction mole\_fraction\_of\_X\_in\_Y, where X is a material constituent of Y.
reckAKl91UlyUP5tT.Name: hfc125
reckAKl91UlyUP5tT.Title: Mole Fraction of HFC125

reckCAAwTMOmsM8uX.Name: expnob
reckCAAwTMOmsM8uX.Title: Sinking Flux of Particulate Organic Nitrogen Reaching the Ocean Bottom

reckHcyE7dp6UIw3M.Description: at surface; includes precipitation of all forms of water in the solid phase
reckHcyE7dp6UIw3M.Name: prsnIs
reckHcyE7dp6UIw3M.Title: Ice Sheet Snowfall Flux

reckI5LPeIL0Gmdu0.Name: tas
reckI5LPeIL0Gmdu0.Title: Near-Surface Air Temperature
reckI5LPeIL0Gmdu0.Variables: AERhr.tas, CFsubhr.tas, Esubhr.tas, 6hrPlev.tas, 6hrPlevPt.tas, 3hr.tas, Amon.tas, day.tas, ImonGre.tas, ImonAnt.tas, Lmon.tas, E1hr.tas, day.tas_junk, day.tas_junk, AERhr.tasSouth30, Amon.tasSouth30

reckKXhWXjG1Oml47.Description: When land use change results in deforestation of natural vegetation (trees or grasslands) then natural biomass is removed. The treatment of deforested biomass differs significantly across models, but it should be straight-forward to compare deforested biomass across models.
reckKXhWXjG1Oml47.Name: fNProduct
reckKXhWXjG1Oml47.Title: Deforested or Harvested Biomass as a Result of Anthropogenic Land-Use or Change

reckS6Whjb0QwXRAN.Description: The linear extent of the cell in the y direction of the horizontal grid centered at t-points (points for tracers such as temperature, salinity, etc.). Not applicable to unstructured grids.
reckS6Whjb0QwXRAN.Name: dyto
reckS6Whjb0QwXRAN.Title: Cell Length in the Y Direction at t-points

reckSGqyw2Lxoxp72.Description: Loss of ice mass resulting from surface melting. Computed as the total surface melt water on the land ice portion of the grid cell divided by land ice area in the grid cell.
reckSGqyw2Lxoxp72.Name: icemIs
reckSGqyw2Lxoxp72.Title: Ice Sheet Surface Ice Melt Flux

reckVVOr3YPAotOoj.Description: In accordance with common usage in geophysical disciplines, "flux" implies per unit area, called "flux density" in physics. The atmosphere convective mass flux is the vertical transport of mass for a field of cumulus clouds or thermals, given by the product of air density and vertical velocity. For an area-average, cell\_methods should specify whether the average is over all the area or the area of updrafts only.
reckVVOr3YPAotOoj.Name: mcu
reckVVOr3YPAotOoj.Title: Convective Updraft Mass Flux

reckXmSOX35AQ8a9J.Description: This is requested only for the emission-driven coupled carbon climate model runs. Does not include natural fire sources but, includes all anthropogenic sources, including fossil fuel use, cement production, agricultural burning, and sources associated with anthropogenic land use change excluding forest regrowth.
reckXmSOX35AQ8a9J.Name: fco2antt
reckXmSOX35AQ8a9J.Title: Carbon Mass Flux into Atmosphere Due to All Anthropogenic Emissions of CO2 [kgC m-2 s-1]

reckajVabxK8k7G1T.Description: chlorophyll concentration from the calcite-producing phytoplankton component alone
reckajVabxK8k7G1T.Name: chlcalc
reckajVabxK8k7G1T.Title: Mass Concentration of Calcareous Phytoplankton Expressed as Chlorophyll in Sea Water

reckksK5r7Vl1xPkR.Description: Residual mass streamfunction, computed from vstar and integrated from the top of the atmosphere (on the native model grid). Reference: Andrews et al (1987): Middle Atmospheric Dynamics. Academic Press.
reckksK5r7Vl1xPkR.Name: psitem
reckksK5r7Vl1xPkR.Title: Transformed Eulerian Mean Mass Streamfunction

reckxKEQ3jvNDwzMG.Description: Total cloud area fraction (reported as a percentage) for the whole atmospheric column, as seen by the  Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS). Includes both large-scale and convective cloud.
reckxKEQ3jvNDwzMG.Name: cltmodis
reckxKEQ3jvNDwzMG.Processing Comment: Standard name changed to clarify definition
reckxKEQ3jvNDwzMG.Title: MODIS Total Cloud Cover Percentage

reckxqjFo3h3jN02H.Description: carbon concentration from additional phytoplankton component alone
reckxqjFo3h3jN02H.Name: phymiscos
reckxqjFo3h3jN02H.Title: Surface Mole Concentration of Miscellaneous Phytoplankton Expressed as Carbon in Sea Water

reckyZogx1fS4wbDv.Description: Flux of nitrogen into the ocean due to deposition (sum of dry and wet deposition), fixation (the production of ammonia from nitrogen gas by diazotrophs) and runoff (liquid water which drains from land).
reckyZogx1fS4wbDv.Name: fsn
reckyZogx1fS4wbDv.Title: Surface Downward Net Flux of Nitrogen

recl339mWbsYVplVM.Description: Integrate 3D emission field vertically to 2d field.
recl339mWbsYVplVM.Name: eminh3
recl339mWbsYVplVM.Title: Total Emission Rate of NH3

recl7cegKbsb1378L.Description: Tendency of specific humidity due to model physics. This includes sources and sinks from parametrized moist physics (e.g. convection, boundary layer, stratiform condensation/evaporation, etc.) and excludes sources and sinks from resolved dynamics or from horizontal or vertical numerical diffusion not associated with model physics.  For example any diffusive mixing by the boundary layer scheme would be included.
recl7cegKbsb1378L.Name: tnhusmp
recl7cegKbsb1378L.Title: Tendency of Specific Humidity Due to Model Physics

reclC8pK6QUEaLxcv.Description: sum of zooplankton carbon component concentrations
reclC8pK6QUEaLxcv.Name: zoocos
reclC8pK6QUEaLxcv.Title: Surface Zooplankton Carbon Concentration

reclKlSbZg8nJuUN2.Description: Upwelling clear-sky shortwave radiation  (includes the fluxes at the surface and TOA)
reclKlSbZg8nJuUN2.Name: rsucs
reclKlSbZg8nJuUN2.Title: Upwelling Clear-Sky Shortwave Radiation

reclPfj9iMJk7YKSk.Description: The total mass of liquid water contained interstitially within the whole depth of the snow layer of the land portion of a grid cell divided by the area of the land portion of the cell.
reclPfj9iMJk7YKSk.Name: lwsnl
reclPfj9iMJk7YKSk.Title: Liquid Water Content of Snow Layer

reclPmMV5edsi2heX.Description: "Content" indicates a quantity per unit area. "Vegetation" means any plants e.g. trees, shrubs, grass. Plants are autotrophs i.e. "producers" of biomass using carbon obtained from carbon dioxide.
reclPmMV5edsi2heX.Name: cVegShrub
reclPmMV5edsi2heX.Title: Carbon Mass in Vegetation on Shrub Tiles

reclUeJe6uEjDN9Pb.Description: Computed as the water flux into the ocean due to flux correction divided by the area of the ocean portion of the grid cell.
reclUeJe6uEjDN9Pb.Name: wfcorr
reclUeJe6uEjDN9Pb.Title: Water Flux Correction

recldzUPATxJ1Kon6.Description: Picophytoplankton are phytoplankton of less than 2 micrometers in size. Phytoplankton are algae that grow where there is sufficient light to support photosynthesis. "Nitrogen growth limitation" means the ratio of the growth rate of a species population in the environment (where there is a finite availability of nitrogen) to the theoretical growth rate if there were no such limit on nitrogen availability.
recldzUPATxJ1Kon6.Name: limnpico
recldzUPATxJ1Kon6.Title: Nitrogen Limitation of Picophytoplankton

reclkSuZQAwQ5OLEt.Description: Computed as npp minus heterotrophic respiration minus fire minus C leaching minus harvesting/clearing. Positive rate is into the land, negative rate is from the land.  Do not include fluxes from anthropogenic product pools to atmosphere
reclkSuZQAwQ5OLEt.Name: nbpLut
reclkSuZQAwQ5OLEt.Processing Comment: CHANGE SINCE CMIP6: parameter name change (variable used to be necbLut)
reclkSuZQAwQ5OLEt.Title: Net Carbon Mass Flux into Land-Use Tile [kgC m-2 s-1]

reclpGqkxLwRLjuWf.Description: Droplets are liquid only.  Report concentration 'as seen from space' over convective liquid cloudy portion of grid cell.  This is the value from uppermost model layer with liquid cloud or, if available, it is better to sum over all liquid cloud tops, no matter where they occur, as long as they are seen from the top of the atmosphere. Weight by total liquid cloud top fraction of  (as seen from TOA) each time sample when computing monthly mean.
reclpGqkxLwRLjuWf.Name: ccldncl
reclpGqkxLwRLjuWf.Title: Cloud Droplet Number Concentration of Convective Cloud Tops

reclrAlrRd4LGh8Hl.Description: Upwelling Shortwave Radiation calculated using carbon dioxide concentrations increased fourfold
reclrAlrRd4LGh8Hl.Name: rsu4co2
reclrAlrRd4LGh8Hl.Title: Upwelling Shortwave Radiation 4XCO2 Atmosphere

recltndyKT2YgdLEU.Atmosphere review comments: Atmosphere team are happy with the technical description of the parameters and confirmed there is precedent for the modis naming convention. The IPO has reached out to the proposer to inform that an accepted physical parameter does not indicate inclusion into the Data Request - the physical parameter must be assigned to a Variable, which in turn must be assigned a variable group and opportunity to ensure inclusion.
recltndyKT2YgdLEU.Name: clmodisiceReff
recltndyKT2YgdLEU.Title: MODIS Ice-Topped Cloud Area Percentage reported on droplet effective radius dimensions

reclw3kzMQRKDLanu.Description: Tendency of air temperature due to longwave radiative heating
reclw3kzMQRKDLanu.Name: tntrl
reclw3kzMQRKDLanu.Title: Tendency of Air Temperature Due to Longwave Radiative Heating

recm3aJsT89IRrgev.Description: SUM of nitrate over all soil layers
recm3aJsT89IRrgev.Name: nMineralNO3
recm3aJsT89IRrgev.Title: Mineral Nitrate in the Soil

recm6DT32SjTLcaPv.Description: Heterotrophic respiration is respiration by heterotrophs ("consumers"), which are organisms (including animals and decomposers) that consume other organisms or dead organic material, rather than synthesising organic material from inorganic precursors using energy from the environment (especially sunlight) as autotrophs ("producers") do. Heterotrophic respiration goes on within both the soil and litter pools.
recm6DT32SjTLcaPv.Name: rhc13
recm6DT32SjTLcaPv.Title: Carbon-13 Mass Flux into Atmosphere Due to Heterotrophic Respiration on Land [kgC m-2 s-1]

recm7LQ6uTAzBqGfr.Description: carbon from additional zooplankton component concentrations alone (e.g. Micro, meso).  Since the models all have different numbers of components, this variable has been included to provide a check for intercomparison between models since some phytoplankton groups are supersets.
recm7LQ6uTAzBqGfr.Name: zmiscos
recm7LQ6uTAzBqGfr.Title: Surface Mole Concentration of Other Zooplankton Expressed as Carbon in Sea Water

recm7dB9GCTra8aGK.Description: Tendency of Specific Humidity Due to Stratiform Cloud and Precipitation and Boundary Layer Mixing  (to be specified only in  models which do not separate budget terms for stratiform cloud, precipitation and boundary layer schemes.  Includes all boundary layer terms including and diffusive terms.)
recm7dB9GCTra8aGK.Name: tnhusscpbl
recm7dB9GCTra8aGK.Title: Tendency of Specific Humidity Due to Stratiform Cloud and Precipitation and Boundary Layer Mixing

recmChsZYXdFYjgRZ.Description: subsurface litter pool fed by root inputs.
recmChsZYXdFYjgRZ.Name: cLitterSubSurf
recmChsZYXdFYjgRZ.Title: Carbon Mass in Below-Ground Litter

recmCwsbOD67u1SmI.Description: Specific mass balance means the net rate at which ice is added per unit area at the land ice base.  A negative value means loss of ice. Computed as the total basal mass balance on the floating land ice (floating ice shelf) portion of the grid cell divided by floating land ice (floating ice shelf) area in the grid cell. Cell\_methods: area: mean where floating\_ice\_shelf
recmCwsbOD67u1SmI.Name: libmassbffl
recmCwsbOD67u1SmI.Title: Basal Specific Mass Balance Flux of Floating Ice Shelf

recmDlcUUZvRJ1ptc.Description: Dissolved iron in sea water,  including both Fe2+ and Fe3+ ions (but not particulate detrital iron)
recmDlcUUZvRJ1ptc.Name: dfe
recmDlcUUZvRJ1ptc.Title: Dissolved Iron Concentration

recmEGDdjm51kBcXZ.Description: Total volume of sea ice divided by grid-cell area, also known as the equivalent thickness of sea ice.
recmEGDdjm51kBcXZ.Name: sivol
recmEGDdjm51kBcXZ.Title: Sea-Ice Volume per Area

recmKIo8jtmK2dFIK.Description: NOy is the sum of all simulated oxidized nitrogen species, out of NO, NO2, HNO3, HNO4, NO3 aerosol, NO3 (radical), N2O5, PAN, other organic nitrates.
recmKIo8jtmK2dFIK.Name: wetnoy
recmKIo8jtmK2dFIK.Title: Wet Deposition Rate of NOy Including Aerosol Nitrate

recmLpsDG7B97fe3f.Description: Calculated in the absence of clouds.
recmLpsDG7B97fe3f.Name: rsutcs
recmLpsDG7B97fe3f.Title: TOA Outgoing Clear-Sky Shortwave Radiation
recmLpsDG7B97fe3f.Variables: CFsubhr.rsutcs, E1hrClimMon.rsutcs, E3hr.rsutcs, Amon.rsutcs, CFday.rsutcs, CF3hr.rsutcs, Amon.rsutcsSouth30

recmRO7rgWJlodRmf.Description: This is defined as "where ice\_free\_sea over sea"
recmRO7rgWJlodRmf.Name: hfevapds
recmRO7rgWJlodRmf.Title: Temperature Flux Due to Evaporation Expressed as Heat Flux out of Sea Water

recmS4KWDihNREstI.Description: Tendency of salt content for a grid cell from parameterized submesoscale eddy advection.
recmS4KWDihNREstI.Name: osaltpsmadvect
recmS4KWDihNREstI.Title: Tendency of Sea Water Salinity Expressed as Salt Content Due to Parameterized Submesoscale Advection

recmW3LyKgTHSlXbx.Description: Mole fraction is used in the construction mole\_fraction\_of\_X\_in\_Y, where X is a material constituent of Y.
recmW3LyKgTHSlXbx.Name: o3
recmW3LyKgTHSlXbx.Title: Mole Fraction of O3

recmd6S2J9INLUl9C.Description: The phrase "change\_over\_time\_in\_X" means change in a quantity X over a time-interval, which should be defined by the bounds of the time coordinate. "Content" indicates a quantity per unit area. The mass content of water in soil refers to the vertical integral from the surface down to the bottom of the soil model. For the content between specified levels in the soil, standard names including "content\_of\_soil\_layer" are used. "Water" means water in all phases.
recmd6S2J9INLUl9C.Name: dslw
recmd6S2J9INLUl9C.Title: Change in Soil Moisture

recmn1IWOZD31w25H.Name: nppOther
recmn1IWOZD31w25H.Title: Net Primary Production Allocated to Other Pools (not Leaves Stem or Roots) as Carbon Mass Flux [kgC m-2 s-1]

recmoL4hWMkIrWwdm.Description: Eastward component of the near-surface (usually, 10 meters)  wind
recmoL4hWMkIrWwdm.Name: uas
recmoL4hWMkIrWwdm.Title: Eastward Near-Surface Wind
recmoL4hWMkIrWwdm.Variables: E3hr.uas, CFsubhr.uas, 6hrPlev.uas, 6hrPlevPt.uas, 3hrPt.uas, Amon.uas, day.uas, E1hr.uas, Amon.uasSouth30

recmpw7oMH30xYKBs.Description: The total calving flux over land ice is a spatial integration of the calving flux
recmpw7oMH30xYKBs.Name: tendlicalvf
recmpw7oMH30xYKBs.Title: Total Calving Flux

recmrtvPegrFbKPUm.Description: The phrase "tendency\_of\_X" means derivative of X with respect to time. "Specific" means per unit mass. Specific humidity is the mass fraction of water vapor in (moist) air. The specification of a physical process by the phrase "due\_to\_" process means that the quantity named is a single term in a sum of terms which together compose the general quantity named by omitting the phrase. A variable with the standard name of tendency\_of\_specific\_humidity\_due\_to\_stratiform\_cloud\_and\_precipitation should contain the effects of all processes which convert stratiform clouds and precipitation to or from water vapor. In an atmosphere model, stratiform cloud is that produced by large-scale convergence (not the convection schemes).
recmrtvPegrFbKPUm.Name: tnhusscp
recmrtvPegrFbKPUm.Title: Tendency of Specific Humidity Due to Stratiform Clouds and Precipitation

recmryrvAPOsu77gT.Description: Growth limitation of picophytoplankton due to solar irradiance. "Growth limitation due to solar irradiance" means the ratio of the growth rate of a species population in the environment (where the amount of sunlight reaching a location may be limited) to the theoretical growth rate if there were no such limit on solar irradiance.
recmryrvAPOsu77gT.Name: limirrpico
recmryrvAPOsu77gT.Title: Irradiance Limitation of Picophytoplankton

recmrywKaf22uEGlh.Description: Precipitation mass flux of water molecules that contain the oxygen-18 isotope (H2 18O), including solid and liquid phases.
recmrywKaf22uEGlh.Name: pr18O
recmrywKaf22uEGlh.Title: Precipitation Flux of Water Containing Oxygen-18 (H2 18O)

recmtKncv0b3DmBdW.Description: Carbon-13 mass content per unit area in soil.
recmtKncv0b3DmBdW.Name: c13Soil
recmtKncv0b3DmBdW.Title: Mass of 13C in Soil Pool

recmu6spHFFwQxiQX.Description: The total dry mass of dust aerosol particles per unit area.
recmu6spHFFwQxiQX.Name: loaddust
recmu6spHFFwQxiQX.Title: Load of Dust

recmucHd1IHhYrwz8.Description: Mole fraction is used in the construction mole\_fraction\_of\_X\_in\_Y, where X is a material constituent of Y.
recmucHd1IHhYrwz8.Name: cfc114
recmucHd1IHhYrwz8.Title: Mole Fraction of cfc114

recmv5ncJ1uA1hQE5.Description: Upper boundary temperature that is used to force ice sheet models. It is the temperature at the base of the snowpack models, and does not vary with seasons. Report surface temperature of ice sheet where snow thickness is zero
recmv5ncJ1uA1hQE5.Name: litemptop
recmv5ncJ1uA1hQE5.Title: Temperature at Top of Ice Sheet Model

recnHeBVVqXLkUlTs.Description: The phrase "integral\_wrt\_X\_of\_Y" means int Y dX. To specify the limits of the integral the data variable should have an axis for X and associated coordinate bounds. If no axis for X is associated with the data variable, or no coordinate bounds are specified, it is assumed that the integral is calculated over the entire vertical extent of the medium, e.g, if the medium is air the integral is assumed to be calculated over the full depth of the atmosphere. The abbreviation "wrt" means "with respect to". Depth is the vertical distance below the surface. Preformed Salinity, S\*, is defined as part of the Thermodynamic Equation of Seawater 2010 (TEOS-10) which was adopted in 2010 by the Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission (IOC). Preformed Salinity is a salinity variable that is designed to be as conservative as possible, by removing the estimated biogeochemical influences on the sea water composition. Preformed Salinity is Absolute Salinity, S\_A (which has the standard name sea\_water\_absolute\_salinity), minus all contributions to sea water composition from biogeochemical processes. Preformed Salinity is the mass fraction of dissolved material in sea water. Reference: [www.teos-10.org](http://www.teos-10.org); Pawlowicz et al., 2011 doi: 10.5194/os-7-363-2011; Wright et al., 2011 doi: 10.5194/os-7-1-2011. There are also standard names for the precisely defined salinity quantities sea\_water\_knudsen\_salinity, S\_K (used for salinity observations between 1901 and 1966), sea\_water\_cox\_salinity, S\_C (used for salinity observations between 1967 and 1977), sea\_water\_practical\_salinity, S\_P (used for salinity observations from 1978 onwards), and sea\_water\_reference\_salinity. Salinity quantities that do not match any of the precise definitions should be given the more general standard name of sea\_water\_salinity.
recnHeBVVqXLkUlTs.Name: pfscint
recnHeBVVqXLkUlTs.Title: Integral wrt depth of sea water preformed salinity expressed as salt mass content

The sum of the quantities with standard names wood\_debris\_mass\_content\_of\_nitrogen, surface\_litter\_mass\_content\_of\_nitrogen and subsurface\_litter\_mass\_content\_of\_nitrogen is the total nitrogen mass content of dead plant material.

Evaluated at the upper boundary of the liquid ocean, including at the lower boundary of sea-ice and floating ice shelves.

A number of reference ellipsoids are defined for use in the field of geodesy. To specify which reference ellipsoid is being used, a grid\_mapping variable should be attached to the data variable as described in Chapter 5.6 of the CF Convention.

rec3SVb9mtR49l4pC.Comment: The method to calculate the mixed layer depth (mlotst) is documented in Griffies et al. 2016 ( <https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-9-3231-2016> ). It is the depth at which density is larger than the density of the first model level+ a threshold of 0.03 kg.m-3 (appendix H24). We propose to make the reference depth 10 m instead of the first model level (note than some modelling groups already did it that way for CMIP6). A recent study based on OMIP (Treguier et al. 2023, <https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-16-3849-2023> )discusses the fact that using the first model level as a reference makes mlotst less comparable with obs (obs-based datasets reference the MLD to 10m because the diurnal cycle is not well-sampled by observations). Furthermore, the difference of the depth of the first model level between different models makes a significant difference in the computed MLDs in some seasons/regions (Treguier et al., 2023).
rec3SVb9mtR49l4pC.Data Request Actions:
New coordinate variable added (dsigmat) to clarify definition.
Added for all 6 mixed layer depth variables.
rec3SVb9mtR49l4pC.Title: Reference level should be 10m for ocean mixed layer depth mlotst

recRGKSaYH2fODfl6.Comment: The barotropic flow is slightly divergent in most modern ocean models, so it cannot be represented by a streamfunction. Griffies et al (2016) note this and suggest submitting an approximate barotropic streamfunction, ∫ U dy in the +y-ward direction starting from inside Antarctica, where U = ∫ ρ u dz is the vertically integrated x-ward transport. The better approach, they note, is to solve an elliptic boundary value problem, i.e. do a Helmholtz decomposition and then provide just the scalar field for the non-divergent part. If the rationale for not doing that is to keep things simple for ocean modellers, then I propose we provide the barotropic transports U and V = ∫ ρ v dz instead of \`msftbarot\` (which is even easier, though 2x the data). Then, subsequent analysis can use either the approximation \`msftbarot\` or the streamfunction part of the Helmholtz decomposition computed from U and V after the fact.
recRGKSaYH2fODfl6.Data Request Actions: msftbarot has actually been used in assessment reports, and the level of detail required to do the inverse problem would not have made that possible.  Thus, the method suggested here is not well matched to the purpose of the streamfunction --Baylor

recd6DlHdYZNiTzyO.Comment:
The idea of these variables is to gather information on the albedo of the ice- or snow-covered surface (for both land and ocean) - this means that if a grid cell is partly covered by ice or by snow, the value should be computed only on the part of the snow or ice cover, respectively, ignoring albedo of the remainder of the land surface. We may therefore have to update the cell measures accordingly.
Furthermore, since ocean and sea ice will have different cell areas, it must be established whether this metric can be covered in one variable (using both cell measures areacella and areacello where appropriate) or whether this should be rather split into two variables - one for ocean, one for land / land ice.
recd6DlHdYZNiTzyO.Data Request Actions: It was decided that the information required can be obtained more reliably by requesting radiative fluxes.
recd6DlHdYZNiTzyO.Title: definition of various albedo metrics to be discussed / potentially updated

recoQt00Dxp8GARAh.Comment:
The Land Use Model Intercomparison Project would like to update the land use categories for all the Lut variables.  The current designations for the Lut variables is Primary and Secondary Land; Crops; Pasture; and Urban.  We would like to update to separate Primary and Secondary Land, so the new list would be Primary Land; Secondary Land; Crops; Pasture; and Urban.  The CF Area Type table will need new definitions for Primary Land and Secondary Land as below.  Note that this pertains to all variables with the designation Lut (I've only included one in the variables box below.

Note also that, as previously, if a model does not represent one of the land use categories, the data for that element should be filled with missing values.  If a model does not distinguish between primary and secondary land, then models should report anything that would be designated as within the primary or secondary land category (i.e., anything in the Primary and Secondary Land area type), should be included in the Primary Lut category.

Primary Land: Primary land is land that has not undergone LULCC (land use or land cover change) due to human disturbance.  This includes natural, undisturbed forests, grasslands, vegetated wetlands, and bare ground.  Note that the categorization as primary land refers to the land management of that area rather than to specific categories of vegetation cover, e.g., this does not refer to the primary and secondary succession of plant species post disturbance.  Reference: Hurtt et al. (2011), Climatic Change, 109 - 117, Harmonization of land-use scenarios for the period 1500–2100: 600 years of global gridded annual land-use transitions, wood harvest, and resulting secondary lands, doi: 10.1007/s10584-011-0153-2.  

Secondary Land: Secondary Land is land that has previously been used for agriculture, pastureland, or urban development and has subsequently been abandoned or which has undergone or currently is undergoing logging.   Note that the categorization as secondary land refers to the land management of that area rather than to specific categories of vegetation cover, e.g., this does not refer to the primary and secondary succession of plant species post disturbance. Reference: Hurtt et al. (2011), Climatic Change, 109 - 117, Harmonization of land-use scenarios for the period 1500–2100: 600 years of global gridded annual land-use transitions, wood harvest, and resulting secondary lands, doi: 10.1007/s10584-011-0153-2.
recoQt00Dxp8GARAh.Title: Add a land use category to the Lut variables

recwAcTjm5B1Ga5e2.Comment:
The variable Ofx.basin in the CMIP6 data request (also in CMIP5 standard output) had flag\_values and flag\_meanings specified. These were listed in the "Structure" record. Ofx.basin is the only CMIP6 variable that uses these CF terms. As the structure record is not being used to define variables in CMIP7, we need to move the information somewhere else. This potentially means adding one or two columns in one of the Air TAble tables. 

1. Add "Flag Values" and "Flag Meanings" columns in the "Physical Parameter" table. These columns would be blank for all other variables, but it is easy to implement.  
2. It may be clearer to use the "Units" table, and rename it "Units and Flags". The examples given for flag\_values and flag\_meanings in the CF Conventions document to not include a "units" value because there is no unit of measure here: each value in the Ofx.basin field is just a flag to be associated with a character value. This means that the value of "units" is redundant for this variable. Placing the flag\_values and the flag\_meanings in the "Units and Flags" table will make it easier to attach a clear explanation of this feature. This will not impact on how the information is exported to MIP Tables. [Note: the "Units" table from the CMIP6 request has not yet been added to Air Table but can easily be imported in option 2 is taken).

The method to calculate the mixed layer depth (mlotst) is documented in Griffies et al. 2016 (https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-9-3231-2016). It is the depth at which density is larger than the density of the first model level+ a threshold of 0.03 kg.m-3 (appendix H24). For CMIP7, we propose to make the reference depth 10 m instead of the first model level (note than some modelling groups already did it that way for CMIP6). A recent study based on OMIP (Treguier et al. 2023, https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-16-3849-2023) discusses the fact that using the first model level as a reference makes mlotst less comparable with obs (obs-based datasets reference the MLD to 10m because the diurnal cycle is not well-sampled by observations). Furthermore, the difference of the depth of the first model level between different models makes a significant difference in the computed MLDs in some seasons/regions (Treguier et al., 2023).

rec60V3WUpMOsNTk4.Title: sigma_t criterion that determines layer thickness

The effective dynamic sea level as if sea ice (and snow) at a grid cell were converted to liquid seawater.  The liquid-water equivalent sea surface which the liquid would have if the ice were replaced by an equal mass of sea water of the density of the surface water in its vicinity. Inverse barometer responses from sea-ice (and snow) loading are removed using equation H3 of Griffies et al, 2016 (<https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-9-3231-2016>). zos is a dynamic sea level should have zero global area mean.
Ocean dynamic sea level is defined by Gregory et al. (2019: [doi.org/10.1007/s10712-019-09525-z](doi.org/10.1007/s10712-019-09525-z) )

recD8lKZ5inAHBZAf.Atmosphere review comments: Atmosphere team are happy with the technical description of the parameters and confirmed there is precedent for the modis naming convention. The IPO has reached out to the proposer to inform that an accepted physical parameter does not indicate inclusion into the Data Request - the physical parameter must be assigned to a Variable, which in turn must be assigned a variable group and opportunity to ensure inclusion.
recD8lKZ5inAHBZAf.Justification for inclusion: The MODIS instrument simulator is capable of producing cloud fraction joint histograms akin to those from the ISCCP satellite simulator, but can further partition them by cloud-top phase. Furthermore, two versions of the joint histogram exist: one that aligns with the cloud-top pressure & cloud optical depth (CTP-COT) dimensions of the existing ISCCP histograms, and another partitioned by cloud droplet effective radius (r\_e) and cloud liquid water path (LWP). This latter version can used in conjunction with cloud radiative kernels to estimate both the SW effective radiative forcing from aerosol-cloud interactions (SW ERFaci) from liquid clouds, and also the relative contributions of the Twomey effect, LWP adjustment, and cloud-fraction (CF) adjustment separately. This is a new technique that adopts a decomposition framework from the cloud feedback literature ([Zelinka 2012a](https://eur05.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fjournals.ametsoc.org%2Fview%2Fjournals%2Fclim%2F25%2F11%2Fjcli-d-11-00248.1.xml%3Ftab_body%3Dabstract-display&data=05%7C02%7CElisabeth.Dingley%40ext.esa.int%7Cd5a18aa3c0c94a4149ea08dcb5730745%7C9a5cacd02bef4dd7ac5c7ebe1f54f495%7C0%7C0%7C638584752864945047%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=0Ie0IdDPCr0pGBxlt0T16HO7vUfyzUbHnPzo1aqUQys%3D&reserved=0) and [Zelinka 2013](https://eur05.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fjournals.ametsoc.org%2Fview%2Fjournals%2Fclim%2F26%2F14%2Fjcli-d-12-00555.1.xml&data=05%7C02%7CElisabeth.Dingley%40ext.esa.int%7Cd5a18aa3c0c94a4149ea08dcb5730745%7C9a5cacd02bef4dd7ac5c7ebe1f54f495%7C0%7C0%7C638584752864952800%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=mlEna4KNYajh34b%2FFpZK4AMBlwGH%2BBb5wlGLbWcfHSs%3D&reserved=0)). It has been used in observations by [Wall 2023](https://eur05.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Facp.copernicus.org%2Farticles%2F23%2F13125%2F2023%2F&data=05%7C02%7CElisabeth.Dingley%40ext.esa.int%7Cd5a18aa3c0c94a4149ea08dcb5730745%7C9a5cacd02bef4dd7ac5c7ebe1f54f495%7C0%7C0%7C638584752864959609%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=QqdnpJwKxh%2BxfOArXdxMbwgIYa5WLrAUzWCY0%2B1V10c%3D&reserved=0), and a manuscript highlighting its first use in a GCM is nearing completion and will be submitted to ACP in the coming weeks.

The phrase "expressed\_as" is used in the construction A\_expressed\_as\_B, where B is a chemical constituent of A. It means that the quantity indicated by the standard name is calculated solely with respect to the B contained in A, neglecting all other chemical constituents of A. "Nox" means a combination of two radical species containing nitrogen and oxygen NO+NO2. "Vegetation" means any living plants e.g. trees, shrubs, grass. recKZgxzep0vyLzZx.Description: The phrase "integral\_wrt\_X\_of\_Y" means int Y dX. The abbreviation "wrt" means "with respect to". To specify the limits of the integral the data variable should have an axis for X and associated coordinate bounds. If no axis for X is associated with the data variable, or no coordinate bounds are specified, it is assumed that the integral is calculated over the entire vertical extent of the medium, e.g, if the medium is air the integral is assumed to be calculated over the full depth of the atmosphere. Conservative Temperature is defined as part of the Thermodynamic Equation of Seawater 2010 (TEOS-10) which was adopted in 2010 by the International Oceanographic Commission (IOC). Conservative Temperature is specific potential enthalpy (which has the standard name sea\_water\_specific\_potential\_enthalpy) divided by a fixed value of the specific heat capacity of sea water, namely cp\_0 = 3991.86795711963 J kg-1 K-1. The zero Joule reference temperature, referred to as bigthetao, is zero degrees Celsius. Conservative Temperature is a more accurate measure of the "heat content" of sea water, by a factor of one hundred, than is potential temperature. Because of this, it can be regarded as being proportional to the heat content of sea water per unit mass. Reference: [www.teos-10.org](http://www.teos-10.org); McDougall, 2003 doi: 10.1175/1520-0485(2003)033<0945:PEACOV>2.0.CO;2. The phrase "expressed\_as\_heat\_content" means that this quantity is calculated as the specific heat capacity times density of sea water multiplied by the conservative temperature of the sea water in the grid cell and integrated over depth.
recKZgxzep0vyLzZx.Justification for inclusion: This is a fundamental aspect of the earth's energy budget (>90% of anthropogenic excess energy is in the ocean), and due to new numerical schemes and vertical discretizations, it is important to calculate it consistently with the model formulation.
recKZgxzep0vyLzZx.Name: chcint
recKZgxzep0vyLzZx.Title: integral wrt depth of sea water conservative temperature expressed as heat content

recMG1IzfOohqI9tA.Justification for inclusion: To unravel reason for model spread in direct aerosol effect

recMG1IzfOohqI9tA.Title: Ambient Particulate Organic Matter Aerosol Absorption Optical Thickness at 550nm

recMJMRiZsG9HgbAG.Description: Mole concentration means number of moles per unit volume, also called "molarity", and is used in the construction "mole\_concentration\_of\_X\_in\_Y", where X is a material constituent of Y. A chemical or biological species denoted by X may be described by a single term such as "nitrogen" or a phrase such as "nox\_expressed\_as\_nitrogen". The chemical formula of sulfur hexafluoride is SF6.
recMJMRiZsG9HgbAG.Name: sf6
recMJMRiZsG9HgbAG.Title: Mole Concentration of SF6 in Sea Water

recMMKiceOyzXUBXm.Description: NOy is the sum of all simulated oxidized nitrogen species, out of NO, NO2, HNO3, HNO4, NO3 aerosol, NO3 (radical), N2O5, PAN, other organic nitrates.
recMMKiceOyzXUBXm.Name: wetnoy
recMMKiceOyzXUBXm.Title: Wet Deposition Rate of NOy Including Aerosol Nitrate

recMMNw6EVh4eT3QX.Description: Flux of carbon as carbon dioxide into the land. This flux should be reproducible by differencing the sum of all carbon pools (cVeg, cLitter, cSoil, and cProducts or equivalently cLand) from one time step to the next, except in the case of lateral transfer of carbon due to harvest, riverine transport of dissolved organic and/or inorganic carbon, or any other process (in which case the lateral\_carbon\_transfer\_over\_land term, see below, will be zero data). This is requested only for the emission-driven coupled carbon climate model runs.
recMMNw6EVh4eT3QX.Name: netAtmosLandCO2Flux
recMMNw6EVh4eT3QX.Processing Comment: Output this variable only if different from nbp due to additional model components (e.g. riverine land-ocean carbon fluxes)
recMMNw6EVh4eT3QX.Title: Net Flux of CO2 Between Atmosphere and Land (Positive into Land) as a Result of All Processes [kgC m-2 s-1]

recMSkjeVq5myQOP4.Description: Total RH of trees in the grid cell
recMSkjeVq5myQOP4.Name: rhTree
recMSkjeVq5myQOP4.Title: Heterotrophic Respiration on Tree Tiles as Carbon Mass Flux [kgC m-2 s-1]

recMWmpLknlDeFO02.Description: Evaporation at surface (also known as evapotranspiration): flux of water into the atmosphere due to conversion of both liquid and solid phases to vapor (from underlying surface and vegetation)
recMWmpLknlDeFO02.Name: evspsbl
recMWmpLknlDeFO02.Title: Evaporation Including Sublimation and Transpiration

recMXPJmwDKgYxaGx.Description: The mass of surface snow on the land portion of the grid cell divided by the land area in the grid cell; reported as missing where the land fraction is 0; excludes snow on vegetation canopy or on sea ice.
recMXPJmwDKgYxaGx.Name: snw
recMXPJmwDKgYxaGx.Title: Surface Snow Amount

recMaWo0hYmG98KXI.Description: Mass of condensed (liquid + ice) water in the column divided by the area of the column (not just the area of the cloudy portion of the column). Includes precipitating hydrometeors ONLY if the precipitating hydrometeors affect the calculation of radiative transfer in model.
recMaWo0hYmG98KXI.Name: clwvi
recMaWo0hYmG98KXI.Title: Condensed Water Path
recMaWo0hYmG98KXI.Variables: CFsubhr.clwvi, E3hr.clwvi, CFday.clwvi, Amon.clwvi, CF3hr.clwvi, Amon.clwviSouth30

recMajlhfCzIiWczo.Description: The surface called "surface" means the lower boundary of the atmosphere. "Downward" indicates a vector component which is positive when directed downward (negative upward). The vertical heat flux in air is the sum of all heat fluxes i.e. radiative, latent and sensible. In accordance with common usage in geophysical disciplines, "flux" implies per unit area, called "flux density" in physics.
recMajlhfCzIiWczo.Name: hfdsl
recMajlhfCzIiWczo.Title: Downward Heat Flux at Land Surface

recMco649jGD4o6yn.Description: Sigma T is potential density referenced to ocean surface. Defined by Sigma T of 0.03 kg m-3 wrt to model level closest to 10 m depth.
recMco649jGD4o6yn.Name: mlotstmax
recMco649jGD4o6yn.Title: Maximum Ocean Mixed Layer Thickness Defined by Sigma T

recMfamkj4SxeNuma.Description: Mole concentration means moles (amount of substance) per unit volume and is used in the construction mole\_concentration\_of\_X\_in\_Y, where X is a material constituent of Y.
recMfamkj4SxeNuma.Name: no3
recMfamkj4SxeNuma.Title: Dissolved Nitrate Concentration

recMfcdv9b4rmmtjl.Description: Contributions to heat transport from parameterized eddy-induced advective transport due to any subgrid advective process. Diagnosed here as a function of latitude and basin.  Use Celsius for temperature scale.
recMfcdv9b4rmmtjl.Name: hfbasinpadv
recMfcdv9b4rmmtjl.Title: Northward Ocean Heat Transport Due to Parameterized Eddy Advection

recMhjJ0Nq9F01BUc.Description: When land use change results in deforestation of natural vegetation (trees or grasslands) then natural biomass is removed. The treatment of deforested biomass differs significantly across models, but it should be straight-forward to compare deforested biomass across models.
recMhjJ0Nq9F01BUc.Name: fDeforestToProduct
recMhjJ0Nq9F01BUc.Title: Deforested Biomass That Goes into Product Pool as a Result of Anthropogenic Land-Use Change

recMnRAfKx0qtbaWM.Description: carbon concentration from the diazotrophic phytoplankton component alone
recMnRAfKx0qtbaWM.Name: phydiaz
recMnRAfKx0qtbaWM.Title: Mole Concentration of Diazotrophs Expressed as Carbon in Sea Water

recMtLm2PnV1mVPjH.Description: Mole fraction is used in the construction mole\_fraction\_of\_X\_in\_Y, where X is a material constituent of Y.
recMtLm2PnV1mVPjH.Name: c3h6
recMtLm2PnV1mVPjH.Title: C3H6 Volume Mixing Ratio

recMvfhbnhgc1oHC9.Description: Growth limitation of calcareous phytoplankton due to solar irradiance. "Growth limitation due to solar irradiance" means the ratio of the growth rate of a species population in the environment (where the amount of sunlight reaching a location may be limited) to the theoretical growth rate if there were no such limit on solar irradiance.
recMvfhbnhgc1oHC9.Name: limirrcalc
recMvfhbnhgc1oHC9.Title: Irradiance Limitation of Calcareous Phytoplankton

recMvg64NKPR5JDc4.Description: Needed to calculate soil bulk turnover time
recMvg64NKPR5JDc4.Name: rhSoil
recMvg64NKPR5JDc4.Title: Carbon Mass Flux into Atmosphere Due to Heterotrophic Respiration from Soil on Land

recMz4uOAC8skoKzp.Description: Geopotential is the sum of the specific gravitational potential energy relative to the geoid and the specific centripetal potential energy. Geopotential height is the geopotential divided by the standard acceleration due to gravity. It is numerically similar to the altitude (or geometric height) and not to the quantity with standard name height, which is relative to the surface.
recMz4uOAC8skoKzp.Name: zg
recMz4uOAC8skoKzp.Title: Geopotential Height
recMz4uOAC8skoKzp.Variables: AERmon.zg, Eday.zg, EdayZ.zg, CFsubhr.zg, Amon.zg, CFday.zg, day.zg, AERmonZ.zg, Emon.zg, 6hrPlevPt.zg, E1hr.zg, 6hrPlevPt.zg7h, 6hrPlevPt.zg_junk, 6hrPlevPt.zg_junk, 6hrLev.zg, Amon.zgSouth30

recMzBZrzlpb3MulX.Description: in each soil layer, the mass of water in all phases, including ice.  Reported as "missing" for grid cells occupied entirely by "sea"
recMzBZrzlpb3MulX.Name: mrsol
recMzBZrzlpb3MulX.Title: Total Water Content of Soil Layer

recMzK5tcAdCCwmNG.Description: Diatoms are phytoplankton with an external skeleton made of silica. Phytoplankton are algae that grow where there is sufficient light to support photosynthesis. "Nitrogen growth limitation" means the ratio of the growth rate of a species population in the environment (where there is a finite availability of nitrogen) to the theoretical growth rate if there were no such limit on nitrogen availability.
recMzK5tcAdCCwmNG.Name: limndiat
recMzK5tcAdCCwmNG.Title: Nitrogen Limitation of Diatoms

recN0Qq89JUXAj705.Justification for inclusion: To quantify air quality and health impacts
recN0Qq89JUXAj705.Name: sfpm1
recN0Qq89JUXAj705.Title: PM1.0 mass mixing ratio in lowest model layer

recN4s4qugN5W60pC.Description: Upper boundary temperature that is used to force ice sheet models. It is the temperature at the base of the snowpack models, and does not vary with seasons. Report surface temperature of ice sheet where snow thickness is zero
recN4s4qugN5W60pC.Name: litemptop
recN4s4qugN5W60pC.Title: Temperature at Top of Ice Sheet Model

recNIXVAaXW6iaC2g.Description: Precipitation mass flux of water molecules that contain the oxygen-17 isotope (H2 17O), including solid and liquid phases.
recNIXVAaXW6iaC2g.Name: pr17O
recNIXVAaXW6iaC2g.Title: Precipitation Flux of Water Containing Oxygen-17 (H2 17O)

recNLJXimXMtLTM20.Description: Fraction of time that convection occurs in the grid cell.
recNLJXimXMtLTM20.Name: ci
recNLJXimXMtLTM20.Title: Fraction of Time Convection Occurs in Cell

recNSSLJeWOx6LlWc.Comments: New CF standard names requested for ocean surface wave peak periods, [Opportunity] Wind driven Ocean Surface Waves
recNSSLJeWOx6LlWc.Description: Wave period associated with the most energetic swell waves (i.e., waves that have propagated away from their generation area). In spectral wind wave models, this represents the spectral peak across part of the two-dimensional wave spectrum, incorporating just swell waves.
recNSSLJeWOx6LlWc.Name: wppswell
recNSSLJeWOx6LlWc.Title: Swell Wave Peak Period

recNSwKsURLXsxq1H.Description: Y-component of the sea-ice drift-induced transport of snow and sea ice mass.
recNSwKsURLXsxq1H.Name: sidmasstrany
recNSwKsURLXsxq1H.Title: Y-Component of Sea-Ice Mass Transport

recNTzmRCj6sEF11l.Description: Top-of-atmosphere outgoing longwave radiation calculated using carbon dioxide concentrations increased fourfold
recNTzmRCj6sEF11l.Name: rlut4co2
recNTzmRCj6sEF11l.Title: TOA Outgoing Longwave Radiation 4XCO2 Atmosphere

recNUWW6n1ZObybAT.Description: Growth limitation of diatoms due to solar irradiance. "Growth limitation due to solar irradiance" means the ratio of the growth rate of a species population in the environment (where the amount of sunlight reaching a location may be limited) to the theoretical growth rate if there were no such limit on solar irradiance.
recNUWW6n1ZObybAT.Name: limirrdiat
recNUWW6n1ZObybAT.Title: Irradiance Limitation of Diatoms

recNXMb3U71wtgB8v.Description: Tropospheric ozone column, should be consistent with definition of tropopause used to calculate the pressure of the tropopause (ptp). Calculated at 0 degrees C and 1 bar, such that 1m = 1e5 DU.
recNXMb3U71wtgB8v.Name: tropoz
recNXMb3U71wtgB8v.Title: Tropospheric Ozone Column

recNlVVQN4VkmU9ZL.Description: Upward shortwave flux from the sea-ice surface to the atmosphere (energy flow per sea ice area). Always positive or zero.
recNlVVQN4VkmU9ZL.Name: siflswutop
recNlVVQN4VkmU9ZL.Title: Upwelling Shortwave Flux over Sea Ice

recNm41PZ4MQZcTrT.Description: Percentage of horizontal area occupied by land.
recNm41PZ4MQZcTrT.Name: sftlf
recNm41PZ4MQZcTrT.Title: Percentage of the Grid Cell Occupied by Land (Including Lakes)

recNs6Wnbk7V4xARJ.Description: be it food or wood harvest, any carbon that is subsequently stored is reported here
recNs6Wnbk7V4xARJ.Name: fHarvestToProduct
recNs6Wnbk7V4xARJ.Title: Harvested Biomass That Goes into Product Pool

recNuMfGeavvrPQ53.Description: Percentage of horizontal area occupied by ocean.
recNuMfGeavvrPQ53.Name: sftof
recNuMfGeavvrPQ53.Title: Sea Area Percentage

recNvusxX8hAlkGAE.Description: Mole fraction of isoprene in air.
recNvusxX8hAlkGAE.Name: isop
recNvusxX8hAlkGAE.Title: Isoprene Volume Mixing Ratio

recNyGjMY59RdfNZq.Description: The relative humidity with respect to liquid water for T> 0 C, and with respect to ice for T<0 C.
recNyGjMY59RdfNZq.Name: hursmax
recNyGjMY59RdfNZq.Title: Daily Maximum Near-Surface Relative Humidity

recO4KhwcuYVTQGco.Description: "Thickness" means the vertical extent of a layer. "Cell" refers to a model grid cell.
recO4KhwcuYVTQGco.Name: slthick
recO4KhwcuYVTQGco.Title: Thickness of Soil Layers

recO6qre16Co8Hn5I.Description: Report missing data over ocean grid cells. For fractional land report value averaged over the land fraction.
recO6qre16Co8Hn5I.Name: cLand
recO6qre16Co8Hn5I.Title: Total Carbon in All Terrestrial Carbon Pools

recO8cZT6Pz7jNbdH.Description: The phrase "square\_of\_X" means X\*X. The ocean mixed layer is the upper part of the ocean, regarded as being well-mixed. The base of the mixed layer defined by "temperature", "sigma", "sigma\_theta", "sigma\_t" or vertical diffusivity is the level at which the quantity indicated differs from its surface value by a certain amount. A coordinate variable or scalar coordinate variable with standard name sea\_water\_sigma\_t\_difference can be used to specify the sigma\_t criterion that determines the layer thickness. Sigma-t of sea water is the density of water at atmospheric pressure (i.e. the surface) having the same temperature and salinity, minus 1000 kg m-3. "Thickness" means the vertical extent of a layer.
recO8cZT6Pz7jNbdH.Name: mlotstsq
recO8cZT6Pz7jNbdH.Title: Square of Ocean Mixed Layer Thickness Defined by Sigma T

recO8f7x8pKLbrTnS.Description: The surface called "surface" means the lower boundary of the atmosphere. "shortwave" means shortwave radiation. Upwelling radiation is radiation from below. It does not mean "net upward". When thought of as being incident on a surface, a radiative flux is sometimes called "irradiance". In addition, it is identical with the quantity measured by a cosine-collector light-meter and sometimes called "vector irradiance". In accordance with common usage in geophysical disciplines, "flux" implies per unit area, called "flux density" in physics.
recO8f7x8pKLbrTnS.Name: rsus
recO8f7x8pKLbrTnS.Title: Surface Upwelling Shortwave Radiation
recO8f7x8pKLbrTnS.Variables: CFsubhr.rsus, 3hr.rsus, Amon.rsus, day.rsus, ImonGre.rsus, ImonAnt.rsus, CF3hr.rsus, E1hr.rsus, Amon.rsusSouth30, Emon.rsus

recO93NG5GaMmwehL.Justification for inclusion: This is eastward wind variable specifically for the CMIP7 land-atmosphere coupling opportunity with 6 vertical pressure levels
recO93NG5GaMmwehL.Name: ua6
recO93NG5GaMmwehL.Title: Eastward Wind

recO9vXbD7PcKM70T.Description: Runoff is the liquid water which drains from land. If not specified, "runoff" refers to the sum of surface runoff and subsurface drainage. In accordance with common usage in geophysical disciplines, "flux" implies per unit area, called "flux density" in physics.
recO9vXbD7PcKM70T.Name: mrrob
recO9vXbD7PcKM70T.Title: Subsurface Runoff

recONamAt733yoiGQ.Description: Total change in sea-ice area fraction through thermodynamic processes.
recONamAt733yoiGQ.Name: sidconcth
recONamAt733yoiGQ.Processing Comment: CHANGE SINCE CMIP6 in Title - CMIP6:Sea-Ice Area Percentage Tendency Due to Thermodynamics CMIP7:Sea-Ice Area Fraction Tendency Due to Thermodynamics
recONamAt733yoiGQ.Title: Sea-Ice Area Fraction Tendency Due to Thermodynamics

recOSkN2GvF2rXdtw.Description: Y-ward mass transport from resolved and parameterized advective transport.
recOSkN2GvF2rXdtw.Name: vmo
recOSkN2GvF2rXdtw.Title: Ocean Mass Y Transport

recOUbjL77KaBzruj.Description: Rate of change of sea-ice mass through melting/dissolution at the ice bottom divided by grid-cell area. Note that this number is always zero or negative since sea-ice growth is collected in sidmassgrowthbot. This is to account for differential growth and melt in models with a sub-grid scale ice thickness distribution.
recOUbjL77KaBzruj.Name: sidmassmeltbot
recOUbjL77KaBzruj.Title: Sea-Ice Mass Change Through Bottom Melting

recOeBKDDNcG7uuF5.Description: Percentage of entire grid cell  that is covered by shrub.
recOeBKDDNcG7uuF5.Name: shrubFrac
recOeBKDDNcG7uuF5.Title: Percentage Cover by Shrub

recOfAswTRLRTZg25.Description: Flux of nitrogen into the ocean due to deposition (sum of dry and wet deposition), fixation (the production of ammonia from nitrogen gas by diazotrophs) and runoff (liquid water which drains from land).
recOfAswTRLRTZg25.Name: fsn
recOfAswTRLRTZg25.Title: Surface Downward Net Flux of Nitrogen

recOfHLnXChKH8tjD.Description: Vertically-integrated amount of silicate in ice algae, expressed in moles of silicon per square meter of sea ice.
recOfHLnXChKH8tjD.Justification for inclusion: Some CMIP7 models now have sea ice biogeochemistry included and are interested in saving these variables. Models that include sea-ice biogeochemistry support closing the carbon and nutrient s' cycles in the sea-ice zone.
recOfHLnXChKH8tjD.Name: sisi
recOfHLnXChKH8tjD.Title: Dissolved Silicon Amount in Sea Ice

recOfftyPzEbB9S3w.Description: "Calcareous phytoplankton" are phytoplankton that produce calcite. Calcite is a mineral that is a polymorph of calcium carbonate. The chemical formula of calcite is CaCO3. Phytoplankton are algae that grow where there is sufficient light to support photosynthesis. "Iron growth limitation" means the ratio of the growth rate of a species population in the environment (where there is a finite availability of iron) to the theoretical growth rate if there were no such limit on iron availability.
recOfftyPzEbB9S3w.Name: limfecalc
recOfftyPzEbB9S3w.Title: Iron Limitation of Calcareous Phytoplankton

recOhYnzD9HY51xQC.Description: Air temperature is the bulk temperature of the air, not the surface (skin) temperature.
recOhYnzD9HY51xQC.Name: tasLut
recOhYnzD9HY51xQC.Title: Near-Surface Air Temperature on Land Use Tile

recOqJQIPp6duKFlU.Description: Surface solar irradiance for UV calculations
recOqJQIPp6duKFlU.Name: rsdsIs
recOqJQIPp6duKFlU.Title: Ice Sheet Surface Downwelling Shortwave Radiation

recOw3dgFHHk4Q420.Description: Total RA of shrubs in the grid cell
recOw3dgFHHk4Q420.Name: raShrub
recOw3dgFHHk4Q420.Title: Autotrophic Respiration on Shrub Tiles as Carbon Mass Flux [kgC m-2 s-1]

recOx1O2DWEjoXj2H.Description: Tendency of heat content for a grid cell from all processes. Reported only for models that use potential temperature as prognostic field.
recOx1O2DWEjoXj2H.Name: opottemptend
recOx1O2DWEjoXj2H.Title: Tendency of Sea Water Potential Temperature Expressed as Heat Content

recP3QXrlJiXRFnCJ.Description: Rate of change of sea-ice mass due to transformation of snow to sea ice divided by grid-cell area. Always positive or zero.
recP3QXrlJiXRFnCJ.Name: sidmassgrowthsi
recP3QXrlJiXRFnCJ.Processing Comment: CHANGE SINCE CMIP6 in Name - CMIP6:sidmasssi CMIP7:sidmassgrowthsi
recP3QXrlJiXRFnCJ.Title: Sea-Ice Mass Change Through Snow-to-Ice Conversion

recP3tC7dzLf0ThAF.Description: Dry Deposition includes gravitational settling and turbulent deposition
recP3tC7dzLf0ThAF.Name: dryso2
recP3tC7dzLf0ThAF.Title: Dry Deposition Rate of SO2

recP92ef9bhW5czSK.Description: Magnitude of basal drag at land ice base
recP92ef9bhW5czSK.Name: strbasemag
recP92ef9bhW5czSK.Title: Land Ice Basal Drag

recPA2zV70jRx8Q1l.Description: Change over time of the mass of water per unit area in the fluvial system (stream and floodplain).
recPA2zV70jRx8Q1l.Name: drivw
recPA2zV70jRx8Q1l.Title: Change in River Storage

recPB29XV1uLjke5s.Comments: "Change names of snow-on-sea-ice terms to start with ""sisn"""
recPB29XV1uLjke5s.Description: Rate of change of snow mass due to sea ice dynamics (advection, divergence, etc.) divided by grid-cell area.
recPB29XV1uLjke5s.Name: sisndmassdyn
recPB29XV1uLjke5s.Processing Comment: CHANGE SINCE CMIP6 in Name - CMIP6: sndmassdyn, CMIP7: sisndmassdyn
recPB29XV1uLjke5s.Title: Snow Mass Rate of Change Through Advection by Sea-Ice Dynamics

recPFHHGH1m3DbGlb.Description: Heterotrophic respiration is respiration by heterotrophs ("consumers"), which are organisms (including animals and decomposers) that consume other organisms or dead organic material, rather than synthesising organic material from inorganic precursors using energy from the environment (especially sunlight) as autotrophs ("producers") do. Heterotrophic respiration goes on within both the soil and litter pools.
recPFHHGH1m3DbGlb.Name: rhc14
recPFHHGH1m3DbGlb.Title: Carbon-14 Mass Flux into Atmosphere Due to Heterotrophic Respiration on Land [kgC m-2 s-1]

recPFeD3szIBE4QL6.Description: Difference in partial pressure of carbon dioxide between sea water and air.  The partial pressure of a dissolved gas in sea water is the partial pressure in air with which it would be in equilibrium.
recPFeD3szIBE4QL6.Name: dpco2
recPFeD3szIBE4QL6.Title: Delta CO2 Partial Pressure

recPFhObArNuQelVQ.Description: Percentage of entire grid cell  that is covered by C3 PFTs (including grass, crops, and trees).
recPFhObArNuQelVQ.Name: c3PftFrac
recPFhObArNuQelVQ.Title: Percentage Cover by C3 Plant Functional Type

recPFrfXJJsLzVkXK.Description: Mass flux of surface meltwater which refreezes within the snowpack. Computed as the total refreezing on the land ice portion of the grid cell divided by land ice area in the grid cell.
recPFrfXJJsLzVkXK.Name: snicefreezIs
recPFrfXJJsLzVkXK.Title: Ice Sheet Surface Snow and Ice Refreeze Flux

recPMB2ADR2tGHw7n.Description: The linear extent of the cell in the y direction of the horizontal grid centered at v-points (points for velocity in the y-direction). Not applicable to unstructured grids.
recPMB2ADR2tGHw7n.Justification for inclusion: To be able to do accurate calculations for the ocean model the width of the gridboxes in both the east/west and north/south direction is essential. This is particularly true if ocean transects are being investigated. Furthermore, attempting to estimate these parameters using the longitudes and latitudes from the t,u and v grid points often leads to incorrect values due to some models artificially narrowing channels (e.g. Strait of Gibraltar and between various islands in the Indonesian Through flow region.
recPMB2ADR2tGHw7n.Name: dyvo
recPMB2ADR2tGHw7n.Proposer name: Jenny Mecking – Ocean and Sea Ice Author Team – National Oceanography Centre – Climate and Uncertainty group
recPMB2ADR2tGHw7n.Title: Cell Length in the Y Direction at v-points

recPVr215QWVxALQd.Justification for inclusion: This is the Omega (=dp/dt) specifically for the CMIP7 land-atmosphere coupling opportunity with 6 vertical pressure levels

Positive and negative numbers refer to total northward/eastward and southward/westward transports, respectively. The transport should be evaluated for the full depth of the ocean, except for the Pacific Equatorial Undercurrent, which is averaged from the surface to 350m.
recQSJHOohmpQp93s.Justification for inclusion: There are a number of climatologically important straits, throughflows, and current systems whose mass transport has been measured observationally. These mass transports provide a useful means of characterizing the rates at which water flows through key regions of the ocean. Offline diagnostics of these transports, using the archived velocity and/or the barotropic streamfunction, can be subject to uncertainty, especially for models with complex horizontal and vertical grids. It is thus more direct and accurate for each participating model group to diagnose transports online.

recTCFcHWIsia7VP2.Description: The phrase "integral\_wrt\_X\_of\_Y" means int Y dX. To specify the limits of the integral the data variable should have an axis for X and associated coordinate bounds. If no axis for X is associated with the data variable, or no coordinate bounds are specified, it is assumed that the integral is calculated over the entire vertical extent of the medium, e.g, if the medium is air the integral is assumed to be calculated over the full depth of the atmosphere. The abbreviation "wrt" means "with respect to". Depth is the vertical distance below the surface. Preformed Salinity, S\*, is defined as part of the Thermodynamic Equation of Seawater 2010 (TEOS-10) which was adopted in 2010 by the Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission (IOC). Preformed Salinity is a salinity variable that is designed to be as conservative as possible, by removing the estimated biogeochemical influences on the sea water composition. Preformed Salinity is Absolute Salinity, S\_A (which has the standard name sea\_water\_absolute\_salinity), minus all contributions to sea water composition from biogeochemical processes. Preformed Salinity is the mass fraction of dissolved material in sea water. Reference: [www.teos-10.org](http://www.teos-10.org); Pawlowicz et al., 2011 doi: 10.5194/os-7-363-2011; Wright et al., 2011 doi: 10.5194/os-7-1-2011. There are also standard names for the precisely defined salinity quantities sea\_water\_knudsen\_salinity, S\_K (used for salinity observations between 1901 and 1966), sea\_water\_cox\_salinity, S\_C (used for salinity observations between 1967 and 1977), sea\_water\_practical\_salinity, S\_P (used for salinity observations from 1978 onwards), and sea\_water\_reference\_salinity. Salinity quantities that do not match any of the precise definitions should be given the more general standard name of sea\_water\_salinity.
recTCFcHWIsia7VP2.Justification for inclusion: This is a fundamental aspect of the changes in the hydrological cycle and their impact on the oceans, and due to new numerical schemes and vertical discretizations, it is important to calculate it consistently with the model formulation.
recTCFcHWIsia7VP2.Name: pfscint
recTCFcHWIsia7VP2.Title: Integral wrt depth of sea water preformed salinity expressed as salt mass content

recYQ7Uivoo6WV4zx.Description: Depth-integrated total heat transport from resolved and parameterized processes across different lines on the Earth's surface (based on appendix J and table J1 of Griffies et al., 2016). Formally, this means the integral along the line of the normal component of the heat transport. Positive and negative numbers refer to total northward/eastward and southward/westward transports, respectively. The transport should be evaluated for the full depth of the ocean, except for the Pacific Equatorial Undercurrent, which is averaged from the surface to 350m. Use Celsius for temperature scale.
recYQ7Uivoo6WV4zx.Justification for inclusion: There are a number of climatologically important straits, throughflows, and current systems whose mass transport has been measured observationally. These mass transports provide a useful means of characterizing the rates at which water flows through key regions of the ocean. Offline diagnostics of these transports, using the archived velocity and/or the barotropic streamfunction, can be subject to uncertainty, especially for models with complex horizontal and vertical grids. It is thus more direct and accurate for each participating model group to diagnose transports online.
recYQ7Uivoo6WV4zx.Name: hfacrossline
recYQ7Uivoo6WV4zx.Proposer name: Patricia DeRepentigny (on behalf of Anne-Marie Treguier and Jenny Mecking)
recYQ7Uivoo6WV4zx.Title: Ocean Heat Transport across Lines

recYQAq7k1jz4gYO2.Atmosphere review comments: Atmosphere team are happy with the technical description of the parameters and confirmed there is precedent for the modis naming convention. The IPO has reached out to the proposer to inform that an accepted physical parameter does not indicate inclusion into the Data Request - the physical parameter must be assigned to a Variable, which in turn must be assigned a variable group and opportunity to ensure inclusion.
recYQAq7k1jz4gYO2.Justification for inclusion: The MODIS instrument simulator is capable of producing cloud fraction joint histograms akin to those from the ISCCP satellite simulator, but can further partition them by cloud-top phase. Furthermore, two versions of the joint histogram exist: one that aligns with the cloud-top pressure & cloud optical depth (CTP-COT) dimensions of the existing ISCCP histograms, and another partitioned by cloud droplet effective radius (r\_e) and cloud liquid water path (LWP). This latter version can used in conjunction with cloud radiative kernels to estimate both the SW effective radiative forcing from aerosol-cloud interactions (SW ERFaci) from liquid clouds, and also the relative contributions of the Twomey effect, LWP adjustment, and cloud-fraction (CF) adjustment separately. This is a new technique that adopts a decomposition framework from the cloud feedback literature ([Zelinka 2012a](https://eur05.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fjournals.ametsoc.org%2Fview%2Fjournals%2Fclim%2F25%2F11%2Fjcli-d-11-00248.1.xml%3Ftab_body%3Dabstract-display&data=05%7C02%7CElisabeth.Dingley%40ext.esa.int%7Cd5a18aa3c0c94a4149ea08dcb5730745%7C9a5cacd02bef4dd7ac5c7ebe1f54f495%7C0%7C0%7C638584752864945047%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=0Ie0IdDPCr0pGBxlt0T16HO7vUfyzUbHnPzo1aqUQys%3D&reserved=0) and [Zelinka 2013](https://eur05.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fjournals.ametsoc.org%2Fview%2Fjournals%2Fclim%2F26%2F14%2Fjcli-d-12-00555.1.xml&data=05%7C02%7CElisabeth.Dingley%40ext.esa.int%7Cd5a18aa3c0c94a4149ea08dcb5730745%7C9a5cacd02bef4dd7ac5c7ebe1f54f495%7C0%7C0%7C638584752864952800%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=mlEna4KNYajh34b%2FFpZK4AMBlwGH%2BBb5wlGLbWcfHSs%3D&reserved=0)). It has been used in observations by [Wall 2023](https://eur05.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Facp.copernicus.org%2Farticles%2F23%2F13125%2F2023%2F&data=05%7C02%7CElisabeth.Dingley%40ext.esa.int%7Cd5a18aa3c0c94a4149ea08dcb5730745%7C9a5cacd02bef4dd7ac5c7ebe1f54f495%7C0%7C0%7C638584752864959609%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=QqdnpJwKxh%2BxfOArXdxMbwgIYa5WLrAUzWCY0%2B1V10c%3D&reserved=0), and a manuscript highlighting its first use in a GCM is nearing completion and will be submitted to ACP in the coming weeks.

recZSVJN5JKGHxTw1.Atmosphere review comments: Atmosphere team are happy with the technical description of the parameters and confirmed there is precedent for the modis naming convention. The IPO has reached out to the proposer to inform that an accepted physical parameter does not indicate inclusion into the Data Request - the physical parameter must be assigned to a Variable, which in turn must be assigned a variable group and opportunity to ensure inclusion.
recZSVJN5JKGHxTw1.Justification for inclusion: This parameter is similar to _clisccp_, the existing 7x7 joint histogram of cloud fraction, partitioned by cloud-top pressure (CTP) and cloud optical depth (COT). This parameter alone is an important metric for comparing the simulation of clouds across models, given the differences between the MODIS and ISCCP instrument simulators (summarized in [Pincus et al 2012](https://eur05.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fjournals.ametsoc.org%2Fview%2Fjournals%2Fclim%2F25%2F13%2Fjcli-d-11-00267.1.xml&data=05%7C02%7CElisabeth.Dingley%40ext.esa.int%7Cd5a18aa3c0c94a4149ea08dcb5730745%7C9a5cacd02bef4dd7ac5c7ebe1f54f495%7C0%7C0%7C638584752864920723%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=ATWFk2FgzgikZKn86KzeC6sZWzk1P7qICZos2SW4bbU%3D&reserved=0)). Furthermore, it is an important supplement to _clmodisice _and _clmodisliquid_, as it can be used to decompose forcing from liquid- and ice-clouds into their "true" components by accounting for obscuration effects (ie, removing the component of aerosol forcing from liquid clouds that comes from changes in overlying ice clouds, rather than changes from the liquid clouds themselves). Furthermore, this metric can be used as output in historical simulations to compare MODIS simulator output from a GCM to MODIS observations to evaluate model performance (as in [Klein 2013,](https://eur05.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fagupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com%2Fdoi%2Ffull%2F10.1002%2Fjgrd.50141&data=05%7C02%7CElisabeth.Dingley%40ext.esa.int%7Cd5a18aa3c0c94a4149ea08dcb5730745%7C9a5cacd02bef4dd7ac5c7ebe1f54f495%7C0%7C0%7C638584752864934620%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=lYOP6ftNOiR%2B64ObT5%2BGRCyd26gOnT%2BxegT2HM3lKT8%3D&reserved=0) but using the MODIS simulator).

recZxONtNdDBgOlrz.Description: The phrase "integral\_wrt\_X\_of\_Y" means int Y dX. To specify the limits of the integral the data variable should have an axis for X and associated coordinate bounds. If no axis for X is associated with the data variable, or no coordinate bounds are specified, it is assumed that the integral is calculated over the entire vertical extent of the medium, e.g, if the medium is air the integral is assumed to be calculated over the full depth of the atmosphere. The abbreviation "wrt" means "with respect to". Depth is the vertical distance below the surface. Practical Salinity, S\_P, is a determination of the salinity of sea water, based on its electrical conductance. The measured conductance, corrected for temperature and pressure, is compared to the conductance of a standard potassium chloride solution, producing a value on the Practical Salinity Scale of 1978 (PSS-78). This name should not be used to describe salinity observations made before 1978, or ones not based on conductance measurements. Conversion of Practical Salinity to other precisely defined salinity measures should use the appropriate formulas specified by TEOS-10. Other standard names for precisely defined salinity quantities are sea\_water\_absolute\_salinity (S\_A); sea\_water\_preformed\_salinity (S\_\*), sea\_water\_reference\_salinity (S\_R); sea\_water\_cox\_salinity (S\_C), used for salinity observations between 1967 and 1977; and sea\_water\_knudsen\_salinity (S\_K), used for salinity observations between 1901 and 1966. Salinity quantities that do not match any of the precise definitions shoul d be given the more general standard name of sea\_water\_salinity. Reference: [www.teos-10.org](http://www.teos-10.org); Lewis, 1980 doi:10.1109/JOE.1980.1145448.

recegrcATeHtiWYGD.Description: In accordance with common usage in geophysical disciplines, "flux" implies per unit area, called "flux density" in physics. "Vegetation" means any living plants e.g. trees, shrubs, grass. "Litter" is dead plant material in or above the soil. It is distinct from coarse wood debris. The precise distinction between "fine" and "coarse" is model dependent. The sum of the quantities with standard names mass\_flux\_of\_carbon\_into\_litter\_from\_vegetation\_due\_to\_mortality and mass\_flux\_of\_carbon\_into\_litter\_from\_vegetation\_due\_to\_senescence is mass\_flux\_of\_carbon\_into\_litter\_from\_vegetation.

receqbow1fsHRNCo6.Description: "Content" indicates a quantity per unit area.

recfembjlk8OdCJyA.Description: The surface called "surface" means the lower boundary of the atmosphere. "longwave" means longwave radiation. Downwelling radiation is radiation from above. It does not mean "net downward". When thought of as being incident on a surface, a radiative flux is sometimes called "irradiance". In addition, it is identical with the quantity measured by a cosine-collector light-meter and sometimes called "vector irradiance". In accordance with common usage in geophysical disciplines, "flux" implies per unit area, called "flux density" in physics.
recfembjlk8OdCJyA.Name: rlds
recfembjlk8OdCJyA.Title: Surface Downwelling Longwave Radiation

Understanding the total flux of calcium carbonate reaching the ocean bottom (as calcite and aragonite) would be important for understanding the ocean sediment response to climate change and ocean acidification.
